pattern: Your picks are quality and workflow verbs for directing an AI on code you don't read line by line: clean it up (polish, lint), set it up (scaffold), check it (code review). New words follow that pattern.

terms.m: Small finishing touches that make something feel finished: spacing, alignment, colors, smooth details. No new features.
terms.w: The app works but looks a bit rough.
terms.p: Polish the home screen: even spacing, aligned edges, consistent button styles. Don't add features.

terms.m: Make something stand out more with stronger contrast, size, or color.
terms.w: A key button or headline is getting lost.
terms.p: Make the Sign Up button pop: bigger, higher contrast, more space around it.

terms.m: Remove extra space, words, or clutter so things feel compact and deliberate.
terms.w: The layout feels loose or the text is wordy.
terms.p: Tighten the card layout: less padding, shorter labels, keep it readable.

terms.m: The layout adapts to any screen size, from phone to big monitor.
terms.w: It looks fine on your laptop but breaks on your phone.
terms.p: Make this page fully responsive. Check 393px phone, 1470px laptop and 2560px monitor.

terms.m: Design for the phone first, then expand for bigger screens.
terms.w: Most of your users are on phones.
terms.p: Build this mobile-first: design for a 393px phone, then scale up.

terms.m: Empty space around elements. More of it usually looks calmer and more premium.
terms.w: The screen feels crowded.
terms.p: Add more whitespace between sections so it feels less crowded.

terms.m: Making the most important thing the most noticeable, then the next, and so on.
terms.w: Users don't know where to look first.
terms.p: Fix the visual hierarchy: title biggest, price next, details smallest.

terms.m: A shared set of colors, fonts, sizes and spacing reused everywhere so the app looks consistent.
terms.w: Different screens look like different apps.
terms.p: Create design tokens for colors, fonts and spacing and use them on every screen.

terms.m: Tiny animations or feedback, like a button press bounce or a checkmark when saved.
terms.w: The app feels flat or lifeless.
terms.p: Add subtle microinteractions: button press feedback and a checkmark when saved.

terms.m: What a screen shows when there is no data yet.
terms.w: A new user sees a blank page.
terms.p: Design a friendly empty state for the list with a short tip and an Add button.

terms.m: Matching a design exactly, down to individual pixels.
terms.w: You have a mockup and want it copied precisely.
terms.p: Match this screenshot pixel-perfect: same spacing, fonts and colors.

terms.m: Something that doesn't work the way it should.
terms.w: Anything is broken.
terms.p: There's a bug: tapping Save does nothing on iPhone. Find the cause and fix it.

terms.m: The exact steps to make a bug happen again.
terms.w: Reporting a bug so the AI can find it.
terms.p: Repro steps: open Settings, toggle Dark, go back. Expected: stays on. Actual: resets.

terms.m: The real underlying reason for a problem, not just the symptom.
terms.w: The same bug keeps coming back.
terms.p: Don't patch the symptom. Find the root cause and explain it before fixing.

terms.m: Something that used to work broke after a change.
terms.w: An update broke an old feature.
terms.p: This is a regression: login worked yesterday. Check what changed and fix it.

terms.m: A quick, urgent fix pushed straight to the live app.
terms.w: Something is broken for real users right now.
terms.p: Hotfix: checkout is down on the live site. Smallest safe fix, ship it now.

terms.m: Reorganize the code so it's cleaner, without changing what the app does.
terms.w: Code is getting messy and the AI keeps breaking things.
terms.p: Refactor the settings page into smaller pieces. No behavior changes.

terms.m: Investigate why something is going wrong, step by step.
terms.w: You don't know what's broken, just that it is.
terms.p: Debug why the images don't load. Add logging and tell me what you find.

terms.m: Error messages the browser logs behind the scenes.
terms.w: A page acts weird and you want a checkup.
terms.p: Open the page, check for console errors, and fix every one.

terms.m: Undo a change and go back to the last working version.
terms.w: A new change made things worse.
terms.p: Roll back the last commit. The previous version was working.

terms.m: Something that fails only sometimes, unpredictably.
terms.w: A test or feature works on and off.
terms.p: The upload is flaky, about 1 in 5 fails. Make it reliable and add a retry.

terms.m: Set up the basic skeleton of a project or feature, ready to fill in.
terms.w: Starting something new.
terms.p: Scaffold a new React app with a home page, settings page and routing.

terms.m: A placeholder piece that pretends to work so you can build around it.
terms.w: A part depends on something not ready yet.
terms.p: Stub the payment step for now: fake a successful payment so I can test the flow.

terms.m: Fake but realistic data used for building and testing.
terms.w: You want to see the design before real data exists.
terms.p: Fill the dashboard with realistic mock data: 20 customers, mixed statuses.

terms.m: Minimum Viable Product: the smallest version that is still useful.
terms.w: You want to launch fast and learn.
terms.p: Build an MVP: sign up, add a task, mark it done. Nothing else yet.

terms.m: A rough version to try an idea, not meant to last.
terms.w: You want to see if an idea feels right.
terms.p: Make a quick clickable prototype of the onboarding. It doesn't need to save data.

terms.m: A reusable building block, like a button or card.
terms.w: The same thing appears in many places.
terms.p: Turn the product card into a reusable component and use it everywhere.

terms.m: The way two programs talk to each other and exchange data.
terms.w: Your app needs data from another service.
terms.p: Connect to the weather API and show today's forecast. Keep the key out of the code.

terms.m: When a page loads as plain content first and then becomes interactive.
terms.w: Buttons don't respond for a moment after load, or content flickers.
terms.p: The page flickers on load. Check for a hydration mismatch and fix it.

terms.m: The information the app remembers right now, like what's in the cart.
terms.w: Things reset or don't update when they should.
terms.p: The cart count doesn't update. Fix how cart state is stored and shared.

terms.m: Connect pieces together so they actually work.
terms.w: The design exists but buttons do nothing.
terms.p: Wire up the form so Submit saves to the database and shows a confirmation.

terms.m: Unusual situations: empty input, very long names, no internet, zero items.
terms.w: Before launch, to avoid surprises.
terms.p: List the edge cases for this form and handle each one: empty, too long, offline.

terms.m: Automatic checks that catch sloppy code and likely mistakes without running it.
terms.w: Keeping code tidy.
terms.p: Run the linter and fix all warnings.

terms.m: Small automatic checks that confirm features still work.
terms.w: You want changes not to break things.
terms.p: Add tests for the signup flow and make sure they pass before you finish.

terms.m: Make something sturdier and safer against bad input, errors and attacks.
terms.w: Getting ready for real users.
terms.p: Harden the login: rate limit attempts, validate input, handle errors cleanly.

terms.m: Doing something twice has the same result as doing it once.
terms.w: Double taps or retries create duplicates.
terms.p: Make the Pay button idempotent so double taps never charge twice.

terms.m: Don't Repeat Yourself: keep one copy of logic instead of pasting it around.
terms.w: The same fix has to be made in many places.
terms.p: This code repeats in 4 places. Make it DRY with one shared function.

terms.m: Shortcuts that work now but make future changes harder.
terms.w: Things are slowing down or breaking more often.
terms.p: List the worst tech debt in this project and fix the top 3.

terms.m: Making the app usable for everyone, including screen readers and keyboard users.
terms.w: You want it inclusive and compliant.
terms.p: Do an accessibility pass: labels, contrast, focus rings, 44px tap targets.

terms.m: How fast and smooth the app runs.
terms.w: Pages feel slow.
terms.p: The page takes 5 seconds to load. Improve performance and tell me what you changed.

terms.m: Checking code for problems before it goes live.
terms.w: Before shipping something big.
terms.p: Review your changes like a senior engineer and list any risks before I ship.

terms.m: Release it to real users.
terms.w: It's ready.
terms.p: Ship it: commit, push, and confirm the live page shows the change.

terms.m: Put the latest version onto the live server.
terms.w: Moving changes from your machine to the internet.
terms.p: Deploy the latest version and send me the live URL.

terms.m: Staging is a private test copy; prod (production) is the real live app.
terms.w: You want to test safely before users see it.
terms.p: Deploy to staging first. Only push to prod after I approve.

terms.m: Commit saves a snapshot of changes; push uploads it to GitHub.
terms.w: Saving progress.
terms.p: Commit with a clear message and push to main.

terms.m: Force browsers to load the newest files instead of old saved copies.
terms.w: You shipped but still see the old version.
terms.p: I still see the old version. Cache-bust the CSS and JS.

terms.m: Use your own product yourself, like a real user.
terms.w: Before asking others to try it.
terms.p: Let's dogfood: walk through the app as a new user and list every rough spot.

terms.m: A switch to turn a feature on or off without redeploying.
terms.w: You want to test a feature with only some people.
terms.p: Put the new checkout behind a feature flag, off by default.

terms.m: A running list of what changed in each version.
terms.w: Keeping track of updates.
terms.p: Add a changelog entry describing today's changes in plain English.

terms.m: A clear written description of what to build: goal, scope, and how you'll know it's done.
terms.w: Starting anything bigger than a small tweak.
terms.p: Here's the spec. Goal: X. Touch only: Y. Done when: Z. Ask questions first if unclear.

terms.m: A checklist that must be true for the job to count as done.
terms.w: You want a clear finish line.
terms.p: Acceptance criteria: works at 393px, no console errors, Save shows a confirmation.

terms.m: What the AI is allowed to change, and what it must leave alone.
terms.w: Stopping the AI from wandering.
terms.p: Scope: only edit the pricing page. Don't touch any other files.

terms.m: Rules and limits that keep the AI from doing something risky.
terms.w: Protecting live data or other projects.
terms.p: Guardrails: never delete files, never touch production data, ask before installing packages.

terms.m: Get it right in a single attempt, without back-and-forth.
terms.w: A small, clear task.
terms.p: One-shot this: add a dark border to all cards. No questions needed.

terms.m: Ask the AI to explain its approach before writing code.
terms.w: Big or risky changes.
terms.p: Plan first: outline the steps and files you'll change, then wait for my OK.

terms.m: The background info the AI needs: files, goals, examples, past decisions.
terms.w: The AI keeps guessing wrong.
terms.p: Context: this is a booking app for salons. Read README and AGENTS.md first.

terms.m: A file in the project with standing rules every AI agent reads.
terms.w: You repeat the same instructions every time.
terms.p: Add these rules to AGENTS.md so every agent follows them.

terms.m: When the AI confidently makes something up.
terms.w: It cites a function or fact that doesn't exist.
terms.p: Don't guess. If you're unsure a library or function exists, check the docs first.

terms.m: Ask the AI to prove the work is done: run it, test it, screenshot it.
terms.w: You've been told 'done' before when it wasn't.
terms.p: Verify it: run the tests, load the live page, and send screenshots.

terms.m: Improve in small rounds instead of all at once.
terms.w: The first try is close but not right.
terms.p: Good start. Iterate: keep the layout, make the header smaller and the text darker.

terms.m: A quick check that the main things still work at all, before deeper testing.
terms.w: Right after a change, before you call it done.
terms.p: Smoke test the app: open every page, tap the main buttons, and tell me anything that breaks.

terms.m: A fast common-sense look to confirm the result makes sense.
terms.w: Something looks too good, too fast, or a number seems off.
terms.p: Sanity check this: do the totals add up and does the page match what I asked for?

terms.m: One round of tidying: remove leftovers, fix naming, delete debug code. No new features.
terms.w: After a feature works but the code got messy getting there.
terms.p: Do a cleanup pass on the files you touched: remove debug logs, unused code and confusing names.

terms.m: Code that is never used anymore but still sits in the project.
terms.w: The project feels bloated or confusing.
terms.p: Find dead code in this project and remove it. Show me the list before deleting.

terms.m: Merge duplicate pieces into one shared version.
terms.w: The same style, function or file exists in several slightly different copies.
terms.p: Consolidate the three button styles into one shared style and use it everywhere.

terms.m: A thorough review against a checklist: security, speed, accessibility, or style.
terms.w: Before a launch, or when you want a full health report.
terms.p: Audit this site for security and accessibility problems. List them by severity, fix nothing yet.

terms.m: Auto-arrange code so spacing and indentation are consistent. Changes look, not behavior.
terms.w: The code looks messy or every file is styled differently.
terms.p: Run the formatter on the whole project. Formatting changes only, no logic changes.

terms.m: A value typed directly into the code instead of coming from settings or data.
terms.w: Changing a price, name or link means hunting through the code.
terms.p: Find hardcoded prices and URLs and move them into one config file.

terms.m: Temporary text, images or values standing in until the real thing exists.
terms.w: You want to spot what still needs real content before launch.
terms.p: List every placeholder still on the site, like lorem ipsum or sample images, and replace them with real content.

terms.m: Standard starter code every project of a kind needs, written the usual way.
terms.w: Starting something new and you don't want to reinvent the basics.
terms.p: Set up the usual boilerplate for a contact form: validation, error messages and a success state.

terms.m: The exact before-and-after of what changed, line by line.
terms.w: You want to see what the AI actually touched.
terms.p: Show me the diff of your changes and explain each one in plain English.

terms.m: A practice run that shows what would happen without actually doing it.
terms.w: Before anything risky: deleting, migrating, sending, deploying.
terms.p: Do a dry run first: list every file you would rename or delete, but don't change anything yet.

terms.m: Move a library or tool to a newer version.
terms.w: A package is outdated, has a security warning, or a fix needs the new version.
terms.p: Bump all packages with security warnings to safe versions, run the tests, and tell me what changed.

terms.m: A safe, separate place to try things where mistakes can't hurt the real project.
terms.w: Testing something risky or experimental.
terms.p: Try this in a sandbox copy first. Don't touch the live project until I approve.

terms.m: Explain the problem step by step out loud; saying it often reveals the answer.
terms.w: You or the AI are stuck going in circles.
terms.p: Rubber-duck this with me: explain step by step what the code does when I tap Save, before changing anything.
